body.statement: For every \(\sigma\in\Sigma_3\), execute the active-allocation handle to derive and display \(\Phi_\sigma\) such that \(P\in\mathcal C_\infty\) if and only if \(\Phi_\sigma(P)\) holds. Each formula must be a finite Boolean combination of inequalities in the six entries of \(P\), contain no latent variable, optimization problem, or unevaluated quantifier elimination, cover every zero-probability and equality boundary, and be paired with an explicit attaining mixture of terminal response-patch laws. The first kill test is the negative-entry class with both off-diagonal probabilities positive: its formula must reproduce exact quadratic support values for all twenty two-patch curves before the exit classes are attempted.
body.justification: The latent-free three-plan formula is the non-generic analytic kernel; it converts a curved iid body into a referee-checkable frontier with constructive boundary attainability.
body.gap: Mbakop warns that iid bodies need not be polyhedral and provides support-function representations, while Pakes et al. use a Jensen outer inequality; neither source eliminates the three-plan turnover body, and separate face inequalities need not be jointly complete.
body.consumer: A three-plan health exchange cell can be screened by displayed inequalities alone, including boundary tables, and every accepted table comes with a structural iid rationalization.

obligation.what_is_open: The unresolved step is the complete latent-free projection for negative entry with both off-diagonal probabilities positive, the zero-sign entry body, and all six exit bodies, including every equality and zero-probability boundary and an explicit attaining mixture in each regime.
obligation.obstruction: The exact negative-entry cone has eight coupled quadratic curve families sharing the same four square-coordinate budgets. When both off-diagonal coordinates are positive, their allocation constraints do not separate: the dual support function has an active switching term involving the smaller off-diagonal mass. Optimizing the face inequalities separately therefore supplies only an outer description, not the necessary-and-sufficient Boolean formula demanded by the open-ended question. No frozen assumption or established result eliminates these coupled allocations, and treating a generic quantifier-elimination output as the requested analytic formula is expressly excluded.
obligation.attempted: The response tables were enumerated by strict-cycle tests for all nine terminal classes. The binary-first-menu reduction was used to enumerate all twenty two-patch curves. Pure rays were removed, the remaining negative-entry and zero-sign cones were reduced to eight and seven nonredundant quadratic curve families, respectively, and the dual minimization over the two off-diagonal coefficients was carried out. Positive-sign entry and the two informative negative-sign boundary faces were eliminated constructively. The remaining route is a finite active-allocation case split for the joint positive-off-diagonal regime, followed by comparison of every resulting support value with exact quadratic maximization over the twenty curves, and then the analogous three-first-choice allocation for exit.
obligation.partial_result:
Relabel the continuing plans \(a,b\), write the path table as
\[
 (A,B,C,R,S,T)=(P_{aa},P_{ab},P_{ac},P_{ba},P_{bb},P_{bc}),
 \]
and put \(\tau=(p_{1a}-p_{1b})-(p_{2a}-p_{2b})\).  Exact strict-cycle enumeration gives the terminal entry response tables
\[
\begin{array}{c|c|c}
&f_1=a&f_1=b\\ \hline
\tau<0&aaa,aab,aac,acc&bab,bac,bbb,bcb,bcc\\
\tau=0&aaa,aac,acc&bab,bac,bbb,bcb,bcc\\
\tau>0&aaa,aac,acc&baa,bab,bac,bbb,bcb,bcc.
\end{array}
\]
For exit, write the lag-choice words
\[
 L_0=bbb,
 \quad L_1=abb,
 \quad L_2=aba,
 \quad L_3=aaa.
\]
The exact permitted indices for first choices \(a,b,c\), in that order, are
\[
\begin{array}{c|c|c|c|c}
\text{initial status}&\operatorname{sign}(\tau)&a&b&c\\ \hline
b\text{ continues}&-&\{2,3\}&\{0,1,2\}&\{0,1,2,3\}\\
b\text{ continues}&0&\{3\}&\{0,1,2\}&\{0,1,2,3\}\\
b\text{ continues}&+&\{3\}&\{0,1,2,3\}&\{0,1,2,3\}\\
c\text{ exits}&-&\{1,2,3\}&\{0,1\}&\{0,1,2,3\}\\
c\text{ exits}&0&\{2,3\}&\{0,1\}&\{0,1,2,3\}\\
c\text{ exits}&+&\{2,3\}&\{0,1,2\}&\{0,1,2,3\}.
\end{array}
\]
Each listed patch is open and nonempty by its strict comparison inequalities.

For positive-sign entry define, for nonnegative \(a,c,s,h,b\),
\[
 \Phi(a,c,s,h;b)=
 \bigl[bc\le h(a+c)\ \wedge\ b^2\le s(a+c)\bigr]
 \ \vee\ 
 \bigl[bc>h(a+c)\ \wedge\ c(b-h)^2+ah^2\le sac\bigr].
\]
Then the complete constructive result already obtained is
\[
 P\in\mathcal C_\infty
 \quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad
 B\le R+T\ \wedge\ \Phi(A,C,S,T;B)
 \qquad(\tau>0).
\]
It includes all zero boundaries without division.  For negative-sign entry, two complete faces are
\[
 \begin{aligned}
 R=0:\quad&P\in\mathcal C_\infty
 \Longleftrightarrow
 S\ge L\ \wedge\ \Phi(A,C,S-L,H;B),\\
 &L=\max\{0,B-T\},\qquad H=\min\{B,T\};\\[2mm]
 B=0:\quad&P\in\mathcal C_\infty
 \Longleftrightarrow
 A\ge L\ \wedge\ R^2\le(A-L)(S+T),\\
 &L=\max\{0,R-C\}.
 \end{aligned}
\]
The maxima and minima expand into two polynomial branches and the proofs allocate rank-one curve masses explicitly, so these are finite Boolean formulas with constructive attainability.

The full negative-entry cone is exactly the cone generated by the four pure rays in coordinates \(A,C,S,T\) and, for \(s,t\ge0\), the eight curves
\[
\begin{array}{l}
(s^2+st,0,0,st,t^2,0),\\
(s^2+st,0,0,st,0,t^2),\\
(s^2,st,0,st,t^2,0),\\
(s^2,0,st,st,t^2,0),\\
(s^2,0,st,st,0,t^2),\\
(s^2,st,0,0,t^2+st,0),\\
(s^2,st,0,0,t^2,st),\\
(0,st,s^2,0,t^2,st).
\end{array}
\]
The zero-sign cone removes the sixth curve.  Thus this reduction is already finite and exact, not an infinite-dimensional residual.  If \(a,c,s,t\ge0\) are dual coefficients on the four pure-ray coordinates and \(b,r\) are the coefficients on \(B,R\), exact nonnegativity on these curves is equivalent to
\[
 r\ge-\rho,
 \qquad b\ge-\beta,
 \qquad b+r\ge-\gamma,
\]
where
\[
 \rho=\min(a,c)+2\sqrt{a\min(s,t)},
 \qquad
 \beta=\min\{s+2\sqrt{as},t+2\sqrt{as},t+2\sqrt{cs}\},
 \qquad
 \gamma=2\sqrt{as}.
\]
For fixed \(a,c,s,t\), minimizing the dual objective over \(b,r\) gives
\[
 -\left[B\beta+R\rho-\min(B,R)\max\{\beta+\rho-\gamma,0\}\right].
\]
The last coupled term proves exactly why the two solved faces cannot simply be intersected to characterize the positive-off-diagonal regime, and it is the computable starting point for the required kill test.
